subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A child has permanent difficulty with muscle coordination and movement due to damage to the developing brain occurring before, during, or shortly after birth, but has entirely normal intellectual ability. This physical condition is called:
explanation: Cerebral palsy is a motor/movement disorder from early brain damage — intelligence is often unaffected, so teachers must avoid assuming cognitive impairment based on physical symptoms alone — distinct from Down syndrome (a genetic/chromosomal condition, trisomy 21, which does affect cognitive development).
